title: A guarantor's liability - how far does it actually extend
p1:
Many people sign as guarantors thinking they are only a backup option.

But the reality can be very different — a guarantor is not just a name on a document; they may carry a serious financial responsibility.
p2:
A common misconception is that the lender must first exhaust all options against the borrower before approaching the guarantor.

In many cases, the creditor can directly seek repayment from the guarantor when the borrower defaults. The guarantor's obligation can be as strong as the borrower's, depending on the terms of the guarantee.
p3:
The surprising part? A guarantor may become responsible not only for the principal amount but also for applicable interest and costs if the agreement covers them.

Before signing a guarantee, it is worth checking the fine print, understanding the amount involved, and knowing that trust alone does not limit legal responsibility.

A signature as a guarantor can create a real financial obligation.
conclusion: Have you ever signed as a guarantor for someone? Should people be more cautious before taking on this responsibility?
